5. To contend that the child victim has lodged a false complaint against him, the applicant has also asserted the fact that the child victim has changed her version, on the different stages of the investigation,
6.
The applicant has also tried his luck by moving the bail application, before the Court of learned .

Thereafter, the applicant has moved CrMPs (M) No. 1483 of 2023 and 2215 of 2023, before this Court, however, those of applications have been dismissed as withdrawn.

7. Apart rt from this, the learned counsel appearing for the applicant, has given certain undertakings, on behalf of the applicant, for which, the applicant is ready to abide by, in case,
ordered to be released on bail, during the pendency of the trial.
8. On the basis of the factual position, as mentioned in the application, a prayer has been made to release the applicant on bail, during the pendency of the trial.

9. Mr. George, learned counsel appearing for the applicant, has also placed on record the copies of the statements of PW-1 (child victim), PW-2 (her mother) and PW-3 (Principal of the School, where,
the applicant was posted), in order to get the relief of bail.

When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein, that on 4 th May,
2023, the child victim has made statement to the police, mentioning therein, that she is a student of 12 th class in of Government Senior Secondary School 'X' (name withheld).
In the year 2022, she was in Class 10 th.
Due rt to lock-down, on account of COVID-19 pandemic, all the teachers used to take online classes.
The child victim was not having the phone, but, she used to attend the online classes on the mobile phone of her mother.
10.1. As per the child victim, applicant-Manoj Kumar, who is stated to be the Drawing Teacher, also used to take online classes from his mobile phone No. 82787 54185.

facts.

11. During investigation, the birth certificate of rt the child victim was obtained from her school,
according to which, her date of birth was found to be 8 th May, 2007.
Thereafter, copies of the birth certificate and pariwar register were obtained from the Panchayat.

In the said statement, the child victim has levelled the allegation of rape, against the applicant,

sentences.text: As per the status report, the applicant was arrested on 9th May, 2023.
He was also medico-legally rt examined.
His mobile phone was taken into possession.
As per the call details obtained, it was found that the applicant and the child victim used to talk with each other.

14. After completion of the investigation, the police has submitted the report, under Section 173 (2)
CrPC.
In the present case, total 26 witnesses have been cited by the prosecution, out of which, three have been examined and one has been given up.

The case is now stated to have been fixed for PWs on 2nd January, 2024, for recording the statements of PWs, mentioned at serial No. 5, 6 and 7.
15.

The prayer, so made in the application, has been opposed on the ground that the applicant had .
committed a heinous offence and has tarnished the pious relationship of a teacher and student, as such, there is a lot of resentment in the society.
16. It is the stand of the police that in case, the of applicant is released on bail, he may coerce the witnesses and allure them to depose in his favour.
rt 17.
On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to dismiss the bail application.

18. First of all, so far as the argument of the learned counsel appearing for the applicant that the child victim has changed her version at the different stages of investigation, is concerned, that aspect is to be considered by the learned trial Court, before whom, the evidence is to be recorded.
19. The learned counsel for the applicant has drawn the attention of this Court to the cross- examination of the child victim, which has been conducted before the learned trial Court.

20. Although, the statement of the child victim has already been recorded as PW-1, but, at the time of .
deciding the bail application, the deposition, as made by the child victim, before the learned trial Court, should not be discussed, as, it is the sole prerogative of the learned trial Court to discuss the evidence, so adduced of before it, to judge the veracity of the statement.

21. At the time of deciding the question of bail, rt the Court should refrain from discussing the evidence, so collected by the prosecution, as the said discussion may cause prejudice to the case of the prosecution or to the case of the accused.
22. In this case, it has not been disputed that the applicant, at the relevant time, was posted as Drawing Teacher, whereas, the child victim was his student.

sentences.text:
23. Considering the allegations, which have been levelled against the applicant, by the child victim,
this Court is of the view that the releasing the applicant on bail would give a wrong signal to the society that after .
committing such a heinous crime, the applicant is still moving freely in the society.
24.
Merely, that the child victim, her mother and the Principal have been examined, does not mean that of the entire prosecution witnesses have been examined.

Keeping in view the stage of the trial, the apprehensions, rt which have been expressed by the police,
in the status report, cannot be said to be unfounded, at this stage.
25. Moreover, while deciding the question of bail, a delicate balance between the individual liberty and larger interest of the society has to be maintained.
26. Considering all these facts, the applicant is not able to make out a case for grant of bail, at this stage.
Consequently, the bail application is dismissed.

27. Any of the observations, made hereinabove, shall not be taken as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case and the learned trial Court shall decide the matter uninfluenced by any of the observations made hereinabove.
